idiom_name: listener registry over ArrayBuffer[Event => Unit] (function values or a listener trait)
implementation_notes: Scala 2.13's collections API no longer ships the mutable Publisher/Subscriber mixins that 2.12 had, so the realization is hand-written: a private ArrayBuffer of function values (or a listener trait when observers need identity or extra operations) with subscribe, unsubscribe and a notify that snapshots the buffer before calling. Function values replace the Observer interface for the common case and the pattern stays a normal class; use a trait when removal needs identity or when the observer carries state. Reactive-streams libraries (Akka Streams, fs2, Monix) implement a different, backpressured model and should be treated as their own decision rather than as Observer.
pitfalls: ArrayBuffer is not thread-safe: concurrent subscribe/unsubscribe/notify needs a lock or a concurrent collection, and holding that lock while calling listeners invites deadlock.

Removal compares with ==, and function values (eta-expanded methods, identical lambdas) can compare equal, so `-=` may remove a different listener than intended - remove by identity (eq) or by a subscription handle.
The callback runs on the notifying thread in list order with no error isolation: one throwing listener aborts the rest unless each call is wrapped.
Listeners in the buffer are strong references: unregister in the same scope that registered, or wrap them so a dead observer can be collected.
